items.grounds: Re-derived both ways at byte tier, every run spliced from the staged verse map. The finding's form reading holds: oshb:Prov.6.12 (7 words) carries the nominal subject אָדָ֣ם בְּ֭לִיַּעַל אִ֣ישׁ אָ֑וֶן and the first participial predicate ה֝וֹלֵ֗ךְ עִקְּשׁ֥וּת פֶּֽה; oshb:Prov.6.13 (6 words) reads קֹרֵ֣ץ בְּ֭עֵינָו מֹלֵ֣ל בְּרַגְלָ֑ו מֹ֝רֶ֗ה בְּאֶצְבְּעֹתָֽיו, three participial forms each with a prepositional phrase, without a subject noun or a prefix- or suffix-conjugation verb of its own, so it cannot stand as a saying, and WEB renders it as dependent relative clauses, “who winks with his eyes, who signals with his feet, who motions with his fingers,” (web:Prov.6.13); oshb:Prov.6.14 (9 words; 1 K/Q note in pmarks_Prov.json, the inline ketiv מדנים before the qere מִדְיָנִ֥ים; 1 paseq seg, count-only) continues the same third-person singular reference from תַּֽהְפֻּכ֨וֹת בְּלִבּ֗וֹ to its finite verb יְשַׁלֵּֽחַ; and oshb:Prov.6.15 opens the apodosis with עַל כֵּ֗ן (that pointing 1 verse book-wide at byte tier; skeleton 2 verses, Prov.6.15 and Prov.7.15), “Therefore his calamity will come suddenly. He will be broken suddenly, and that without remedy.” (web:Prov.6.15). The shipped row itself describes the span as a chain of participial clauses sharing one grammatical subject and resolved by the causal clause, yet rejects single_proverb because the cohesion runs across four verses rather than a single couplet - a verse-count ground that the ruled continuous-sentence precedent (one syntactically continuous sentence spanning verses is one proverb-unit typed single_proverb regardless of verse count) expressly removes - while proverb_cluster asserts atomic sayings cohering, which none of these member verses are. Warrant defect, not load-bearing: the span is untouched. Both sides weighed from bytes: the preceding unit closes at oshb:Prov.6.11, וּבָֽא כִמְהַלֵּ֥ךְ רֵאשֶׁ֑ךָ וּ֝מַחְסֹֽרְךָ֗ כְּאִ֣ישׁ מָגֵֽן, petuchah-closed in WLC (pmarks_Prov.json PE at Prov.6.11; tier-3, single witness), sharing no skeleton token with 6:12, the address mode shifting from second-person imperative and interrogative to third-person portrait; the following unit opens at oshb:Prov.6.16, שֶׁשׁ הֵ֭נָּה שָׂנֵ֣א יְהוָ֑ה וְ֝שֶׁ֗בַע תועבות תּוֹעֲבַ֥ת נַפְשֽׁוֹ, the six-and-seven numerical formula (1 K/Q note there too, the inline ketiv תועבות before the qere תּוֹעֲבַ֥ת), sharing no skeleton token with 6:15, which is itself petuchah-closed (PE at Prov.6.15; tier-3, single witness). The causal opener at 6:15 and the numerical onset at 6:16 decide; the marks corroborate only. Machine witness: check_universals over the shipped row is GREEN, so no digit gate is implicated. Verdict confirm at medium. The proposed type repair (single_proverb, span Prov.6.12-Prov.6.15 unchanged, dependent fields re-opened) is endorsed as a PROPOSAL with this qualification: the precedent was ruled on a two-verse simile in the Hezekiah collection, and applying it to a four-verse portrait in the lecture collection is a ruling applied rather than a byte fact, so the owner may alternatively type the portrait as wisdom_poem under the closed vocabulary; either way the shipped rejection of single_proverb on verse count cannot stand, and proverb_cluster does not describe these bytes.

Both sides of the forward seam re-derived at byte tier from the staged verse map: the row's closing verse oshb:Prov.10.32 reads שִׂפְתֵ֣י צַ֭דִּיק יֵדְע֣וּן רָצ֑וֹן וּפִ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים תַּהְפֻּכֽוֹת (7 words; atnach U+0591 on word 4, רָצ֑וֹן, colon-final), and the following row's opening verse oshb:Prov.11.1 reads מֹאזְנֵ֣י מִ֭רְמָה תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וְאֶ֖בֶן שְׁלֵמָ֣ה רְצוֹנֽוֹ (7 words; closing word רְצוֹנֽוֹ). The finding's object and digits re-sweep exactly with the staged sweep tool: the final-nun skeleton spelling רצון stands in 8 verses book-wide (Prov.8.35, Prov.10.32, Prov.11.27, Prov.12.2, Prov.14.9, Prov.14.35, Prov.16.13, Prov.18.22; verse counts), the medial-nun suffixed spelling רצונו in 6 verses (Prov.11.1, Prov.11.20, Prov.12.22, Prov.15.8, Prov.16.15, Prov.19.12), a medial-nun sweep of the bare stem רצונ returning those same 6, the two sets disjoint (14 verses combined), and Prov.10.32 with Prov.11.1 the sole adjacent pair among the 14 (chapter 10 ends at verse 32 in both witnesses, so the two are consecutive verses). The row's own primary object re-sweeps at skeleton תהפכות 9 verses book-wide (Prov.2.12, Prov.2.14, Prov.6.14, Prov.8.13, Prov.10.31, Prov.10.32, Prov.16.28, Prov.16.30, Prov.23.33; verse counts) with Prov.10.31-Prov.10.32 the sole adjacent pair, so the straddling favour noun is an argument of the same form the row builds on, and it is undisclosed on both sides of the seam. Tested against the row: the rationale and device_notes both ground the forward edge on the pair closing the chapter's run, and the chapter division is tier-4 metadata that can neither drive nor corroborate a seam; no byte ground for the forward edge is stated anywhere in the row, whose rejection sentence weighs the back edge alone. Which ruled object holds the edge notwithstanding: at skeleton tier 10:32 and 11:1 share no exact token, both of the row's cohesion objects (the perversities noun and the speech-organ-of-the-righteous construct opener) are absent from 11:1, and 11:1 opens on the commerce construct מֹאזְנֵ֣י מִ֭רְמָה under the abomination-of-YHWH and his-delight formula pair, so the edge stands on the row's cohesion objects stopping there, and no merge follows. Back seam weighed for completeness: oshb:Prov.10.30 reads צַדִּ֣יק לְעוֹלָ֣ם בַּל יִמּ֑וֹט וּ֝רְשָׁעִ֗ים לֹ֣א יִשְׁכְּנוּ אָֽרֶץ, sharing with 10:31 the righteous noun alone (skeleton צדיק, 66 verses book-wide, verse counts), a frequent texture token that is neither of the row's objects, so the rejection's back-edge ground is byte-true. Verdict confirm at medium: a defective warrant (a tier-4 chapter close named where the byte ground belongs, with a same-class catchword undisclosed at that seam), not alone load-bearing. The proposed field repair is endorsed as a PROPOSAL with one qualification: the adjoining row argues the same seam with the same undisclosed straddler and the same chapter-division wording in its rejection sentence, so under the seam-pair rule the disclosure belongs on both rows as one edit, which is owner-triage input beyond this item's own row.

Both sides of the back seam re-derived at byte tier from the staged verse map: the preceding row's verse oshb:Prov.11.4 reads לֹא יוֹעִ֣יל ה֭וֹן בְּי֣וֹם עֶבְרָ֑ה וּ֝צְדָקָ֗ה תַּצִּ֥יל מִמָּֽוֶת (8 words; atnach on word 5), this row's opening verse oshb:Prov.11.5 reads צִדְקַ֣ת תָּ֭מִים תְּיַשֵּׁ֣ר דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וּ֝בְרִשְׁעָת֗וֹ יִפֹּ֥ל רָשָֽׁע, and its second member oshb:Prov.11.6 reads צִדְקַ֣ת יְ֭שָׁרִים תַּצִּילֵ֑ם וּ֝בְהַוַּ֗ת בֹּגְדִ֥ים יִלָּכֵֽדוּ. Digits re-sweep exactly with the staged tool: the deliverance verb skeleton תציל stands in 5 verses book-wide (Prov.10.2, Prov.11.4, Prov.11.6, Prov.19.19, Prov.23.14; verse counts); the construct spelling צדקת in 2 verses (Prov.11.5, Prov.11.6), byte-identical as צִדְקַ֣ת and verse-initial in both; and the 11:4 B-colon וּ֝צְדָקָ֗ה תַּצִּ֥יל מִמָּֽוֶת is byte-identical to Prov.10.2 (2 verses book-wide at byte tier). So 11:4 carries the virtue-delivers half of the template with the very verb of 11:6, and the rejection's denial is over-broad exactly as filed. Tested further against the row, the denial fails on a verse the finding did not reach: oshb:Prov.11.3 reads תֻּמַּ֣ת יְשָׁרִ֣ים תַּנְחֵ֑ם וְסֶ֖לֶף בּוֹגְדִ֣ים ושדם יְשָׁדֵּֽם (1 K/Q note; the inline ketiv ושדם before the qere יְשָׁדֵּֽם) and carries the whole virtue-guides / vice-destroys template - virtue construct plus group noun plus 3mp-suffixed guiding verb, then waw plus vice construct plus group noun plus 3mp-suffixed destroying verb - in the very shape 11:6 repeats, with the same group nouns: ישרים at skeleton tier 23 verses book-wide (Prov.11.3 and Prov.11.6 among them), the treacherous noun in its plene spelling בוגדים 3 verses (Prov.2.22, Prov.11.3, Prov.23.28) and its defective spelling בגדים 3 verses (Prov.11.6, Prov.13.2, Prov.13.15), swept per attested spelling. The claim that the template is shared by 11:5 and 11:6 alone is therefore byte-false at 11:3 and half-false at 11:4, and a template running 11:3-11:6 straddles the row's back seam undisclosed by this row and by the adjoining row, whose rejection speaks of wealth/wrath vocabulary and its repeated B-line alone. Which ruled object holds the edge: the exclusive verse-initial construct opener (byte tier, 2 verses, both inside the span) is absent from 11:4, which opens לֹא יוֹעִ֣יל ה֭וֹן and carries the absolute noun וּ֝צְדָקָ֗ה, and absent from 11:3, whose opener is תֻּמַּ֣ת; at skeleton tier 11:4 and 11:5 share no exact token, so the edge stands on the row's driver and no span change follows here. Forward seam weighed: oshb:Prov.11.7 reads בְּמ֤וֹת אָדָ֣ם רָ֭שָׁע תֹּאבַ֣ד תִּקְוָ֑ה וְתוֹחֶ֖לֶת אוֹנִ֣ים אָבָֽדָה, sharing no skeleton token with 11:6, so the forward rejection ground is byte-true. Verdict confirm at medium: a defective rival-rejection warrant, not alone load-bearing, since the driver holds. The proposed field repair is endorsed as a PROPOSAL with the qualification that the restated rejection must reckon with 11:3 as well as 11:4, and with this record for owner triage: the rival extension 11:3-11:6 (the template at 11:3, 11:5 and 11:6, its virtue-delivers half at 11:4 with 11:6's verb) is a byte-arguable candidate the shipped rows never weigh; it is not ruled here, because no span change is before this item.

Both sides of the back seam re-derived at byte tier from the staged verse map: the preceding row's verse oshb:Prov.11.24 reads יֵ֣שׁ מְ֭פַזֵּר וְנוֹסָ֥ף ע֑וֹד וְחוֹשֵׂ֥ךְ מִ֝יֹּ֗שֶׁר אַךְ לְמַחְסֽוֹר (8 words; atnach on word 4, ע֑וֹד), “There is one who scatters, and increases yet more. There is one who withholds more than is appropriate, but gains poverty.” (web:Prov.11.24), this row's opening verse oshb:Prov.11.25 reads נֶֽפֶשׁ בְּרָכָ֥ה תְדֻשָּׁ֑ן וּ֝מַרְוֶ֗ה גַּם ה֥וּא יוֹרֶֽא, and its second member oshb:Prov.11.26 reads מֹ֣נֵֽעַ בָּ֭ר יִקְּבֻ֣הוּ לְא֑וֹם וּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה לְרֹ֣אשׁ מַשְׁבִּֽיר. The pattern the row offers as cohesion evidence beyond the noun - giving rewarded, withholding punished - is byte-present in 11:24 (the scatterer מְ֭פַזֵּר increases, the withholder וְחוֹשֵׂ֥ךְ comes to want), in 11:25 (the generous soul fattened, the waterer watered) and in 11:26 (the grain-withholder מֹ֣נֵֽעַ cursed, the seller מַשְׁבִּֽיר blessed), and it is carried by a different lexeme in each verse: skeleton מפזר 1 verse book-wide (Prov.11.24), חושך 3 verses (Prov.11.24, Prov.13.24, Prov.17.27), מנע 6 verses (Prov.11.26 among them), משביר 1 verse (Prov.11.26); at skeleton tier 11:24 and 11:25 share no exact token, nor do 11:25 and 11:26. So the pattern is theme rather than a construction or catchword, and it does not stop at the row's back edge, which under the collection's ruled cluster bar makes it texture rather than cohesion evidence; offered as evidence, it is a defective warrant claim, and its continuation into 11:24 is undisclosed by this row (the adjoining row even calls its own verse distinct from the giving imagery that follows). The noun the row stands on re-sweeps exactly: skeleton ברכה 3 verses book-wide (Prov.10.7, Prov.11.25, Prov.11.26; verse counts), Prov.11.25-Prov.11.26 the sole adjacent pair, in the forms בְּרָכָ֥ה and וּ֝בְרָכָ֗ה here and prefixed at 10:7 as the row states, with the construct spelling ברכת (3 verses: Prov.10.22, Prov.11.11, Prov.24.25) rightly excluded. Which ruled object decides the back edge: that noun, absent from 11:24, together with the construction shift from 11:24's existential יֵ֣שׁ pair to 11:25's nominal opener; both rows reject the merge on the noun, so the seam is argued coherently and no span change follows. Forward seam weighed: oshb:Prov.11.27 reads שֹׁ֣חֵֽר ט֭וֹב יְבַקֵּ֣שׁ רָצ֑וֹן וְדֹרֵ֖שׁ רָעָ֣ה תְבוֹאֶֽנּוּ, sharing no skeleton token with 11:26 (its favour noun רָצ֑וֹן is unrelated to the pair's noun), so the forward edge is clean. Verdict confirm at medium: a defective warrant, not load-bearing, since the noun holds the cluster at the medium_low confidence and frontier flag the row already carries. The proposed demotion of the pattern to disclosed texture continuing into 11:24 is endorsed as a PROPOSAL, with the note that after repair the row's stated evidence is a one-token chain and its confidence must stay at or below medium_low.

Re-derived at byte tier, both verses spliced in full from the staged verse map: oshb:Prov.12.18 reads יֵ֣שׁ בּ֭וֹטֶה כְּמַדְקְר֣וֹת חָ֑רֶב וּלְשׁ֖וֹן חֲכָמִ֣ים מַרְפֵּֽא - 7 words, atnach U+0591 on word 4 (חָ֑רֶב), the tongue noun וּלְשׁ֖וֹן standing as word 5, first word of the B-colon and third from the verse end, the verse closing on מַרְפֵּֽא; oshb:Prov.12.19 reads שְֽׂפַת אֱ֭מֶת תִּכּ֣וֹן לָעַ֑ד וְעַד אַ֝רְגִּ֗יעָה לְשׁ֣וֹן שָֽׁקֶר - 8 words, atnach on word 4 (לָעַ֑ד), the tongue noun לְשׁ֣וֹן standing as word 7, second-to-last in the verse and in its B-colon, the verse closing on שָֽׁקֶר. So the rationale's leading statement that both verses close on the noun is byte-false for both, and the device_notes clause that the noun sits as the second-to-last word of its own colon in both verses is byte-false for 12:18, where it is colon-initial; the two statements also contradict each other inside one row. Machine witness re-run: check_universals over the shipped row flags that device_notes clause (claim 'last', path device_notes) as a positional universal without a digit-bearing sweep in its sentence, as the finding reports. The shared object itself survives: the two byte forms וּלְשׁ֖וֹן and לְשׁ֣וֹן differ at byte tier (prefix waw and accent) and agree on the noun from accent-stripped tier down, and the skeleton substring לשון stands in 16 verses book-wide (verse counts) with Prov.12.18-Prov.12.19 the sole adjacent pair, so the boundary is unaffected; the rationale's wording 'exact same noun ... byte tier' over two different byte forms is a tier-labelling looseness of the same kind, noted, not separately severitied. Verdict confirm at medium: a byte-false warrant statement that is not load-bearing. The proposed field repair (restate the noun as B-colon in both verses, colon-initial at oshb:Prov.12.18 word 5 of 7 and second-to-last at oshb:Prov.12.19 word 7 of 8) re-derives exactly and is endorsed as a PROPOSAL. both_sides_assessed is false because this item concerns a positional statement inside the span and no seam.

Both sides of the back seam re-derived at byte tier from the staged verse map: the preceding row's verse oshb:Prov.12.17 reads יָפִ֣יחַ אֱ֭מוּנָה יַגִּ֣יד צֶ֑דֶק וְעֵ֖ד שְׁקָרִ֣ים מִרְמָֽה, this row's opening verse oshb:Prov.12.18 reads יֵ֣שׁ בּ֭וֹטֶה כְּמַדְקְר֣וֹת חָ֑רֶב וּלְשׁ֖וֹן חֲכָמִ֣ים מַרְפֵּֽא, and its second member oshb:Prov.12.19 reads שְֽׂפַת אֱ֭מֶת תִּכּ֣וֹן לָעַ֑ד וְעַד אַ֝רְגִּ֗יעָה לְשׁ֣וֹן שָֽׁקֶר. The falsehood noun re-sweeps exactly with the staged tool: skeleton שקר 20 verses book-wide (Prov.6.17, Prov.6.19, Prov.10.18, Prov.11.18, Prov.12.17, Prov.12.19, Prov.12.22, Prov.13.5, Prov.14.5, Prov.17.4, Prov.17.7, Prov.19.5, Prov.19.9, Prov.20.17, Prov.21.6, Prov.25.14, Prov.25.18, Prov.26.28, Prov.29.12, Prov.31.30; verse counts), standing as שְׁקָרִ֣ים at 12:17 and שָֽׁקֶר at 12:19 and absent from 12:18, so the tie skips the seam verse. The adjoining row's rejection states that its verse shares no lexeme with either member of this span; that is byte-false for 12:19 (one lexeme in two number forms), while this row's device_notes discloses the recurrence and holds its boundary, so the corpus carries two incompatible accounts of one object at one seam, as filed. Which ruled object decides the seam: at skeleton tier 12:17 and 12:18 share no exact token, and the row's tongue-noun chain begins at 12:18 (that noun stands in 16 verses book-wide, Prov.12.18-Prov.12.19 the sole adjacent pair), so the atomic boundary at 12:17/12:18 holds on the cohesion object starting there and no span change follows. Also checked so that nothing is overstated: the one exact skeleton token 12:17 and 12:19 share is ועד, a homograph (וְעֵ֖ד witness against וְעַד until) that is no lexeme tie, and the truth nouns אֱ֭מוּנָה (skeleton אמונה, 2 verses book-wide) and אֱ֭מֶת (skeleton אמת, 11 verses) are distinct nouns of one root, a semantic echo neither row claims. Forward seam weighed: oshb:Prov.12.20 reads מִ֭רְמָה בְּלֶב חֹ֣רְשֵׁי רָ֑ע וּֽלְיֹעֲצֵ֖י שָׁל֣וֹם שִׂמְחָֽה, sharing no skeleton token with 12:19 (its deceit noun מִ֭רְמָה echoes 12:17's מִרְמָֽה non-adjacently, as the following row discloses). Verdict confirm at medium: a false cross-row claim, not alone load-bearing. The proposed seam-pair repair is endorsed as a PROPOSAL: this row's disclosure stands as the byte-true account, and the adjoining row's no-shared-lexeme sentence is the side to correct, naming the falsehood noun at Prov.12.17 and Prov.12.19 (skeleton, 20 verses book-wide, verse counts) while keeping the immediate junction's no-shared-token ground; the seam is ruled coherently for both rows with spans unchanged.

Re-derived at byte tier from the staged verse map: oshb:Prov.14.12 reads יֵ֤שׁ דֶּ֣רֶךְ יָ֭שָׁר לִפְנֵי אִ֑ישׁ וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ דַּרְכֵי מָֽוֶת (8 words; atnach U+0591 on word 5, אִ֑ישׁ; hinge word וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ as word 6, first word of the B-colon) and oshb:Prov.14.13 reads גַּם בִּשְׂח֥וֹק יִכְאַב לֵ֑ב וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ שִׂמְחָ֣ה תוּגָֽה (7 words; atnach on word 4, לֵ֑ב; hinge word וְאַחֲרִיתָ֖הּ as word 5, first word of the B-colon). The two hinge forms differ at byte tier (accents) and agree from accent-stripped tier down; the skeleton ואחריתה stands in 5 verses book-wide (Prov.5.4, Prov.14.12, Prov.14.13, Prov.16.25, Prov.20.21; verse counts) with Prov.14.12-Prov.14.13 the sole adjacent pair, and 14:12 is byte-identical to Prov.16.25 in full, as the row discloses. Tested against the finding: the appearance-versus-outcome template is not tier-4 metadata and not English-only cohesion, because it is realised in the bytes as one construction in both verses - an A-colon observation, the atnach, the same hinge word colon-initial, then a nominal outcome (דַּרְכֵי מָֽוֶת; שִׂמְחָ֣ה תוּגָֽה) - which is the accent-tier fact the finding itself names as genuinely independent and the row's observed_substrate_signals already assert as the B-colon pivot. Tested against the row: as written, the rationale's first ground already includes the pivot function, so the second ground labelled independent restates it in English semantic dress, names no tier and no byte fact, and carries the universal 'identical' without a digit-bearing sweep in its sentence, which check_universals re-run over the shipped row flags at boundary_rationale exactly as the finding reports. The row's medium confidence rests on the first ground (the operative hinge word in the same colon slot), which is byte-true, so nothing load-bearing turns on the second ground and no calibration changes. Both sides weighed: oshb:Prov.14.11 reads בֵּ֣ית רְ֭שָׁעִים יִשָּׁמֵ֑ד וְאֹ֖הֶל יְשָׁרִ֣ים יַפְרִֽיחַ, sharing no skeleton token with 14:12; oshb:Prov.14.14 reads מִדְּרָכָ֣יו יִ֭שְׂבַּע ס֣וּג לֵ֑ב וּ֝מֵעָלָ֗יו אִ֣ישׁ טֽוֹב, sharing with 14:13 the heart noun לֵ֑ב alone, the atnach word of both (that byte form 13 verses book-wide, verse counts), a frequent texture token carrying no part of the hinge object; the hinge word is absent from both neighbours, so the cluster object stops at both edges and no span question arises.
